# Validation (M6): current status

**Read this first.** Results in this project come from **synthetic** documents generated by `src/taadeel/synthetic.py` with known operations, and from a small sample of real English UK legislation. They measure whether the engine recovers operations it was given. They do **not** measure accuracy on real UAE legislation. A hand checked real gold set (cited per item) is **not yet built** because no source currently permits text collection (see `DATA_SOURCES.md`). Until it exists, claims about real world accuracy must not be made.

## Where the numbers are

This file holds no hand typed result figures. Numbers live only in generated files:

* `docs/HELDOUT_RESULTS.md` (generated): held out synthetic results.
* `docs/VALIDATION_UK.md` (generated): UK English validation.
* `results/dev_synthetic.json`: synthetic development results.

Reproduce the development table with `python -m taadeel.validate table 30` (seeds 0 to 29 per scenario). Scenarios range from an easy case (random text, small edits) to templated near duplicate text with small edits, 40% or 70% of words edited, and many inserts and repeals.

## What this shows (qualitative)

1. **The easy scenario is uninformative.** Perfect scores arise because random text from a large word pool makes articles trivially distinguishable. It stays only as a sanity check.
2. **Near duplicate articles are the real difficulty.** When articles share most of their wording (templated text, which resembles boilerplate heavy statutes), a repealed article is often matched to a similar neighbour. An ambiguity check was added so that such pairs are marked `low` confidence. They are still *aligned*, so recall for `repealed` and `inserted` drops: the engine reports them as `replaced` with low confidence instead of repealed plus inserted.
3. **Heavy rewrites degrade alignment.** Text similarity cannot distinguish a heavily rewritten article from a repeal plus an unrelated insertion; structural position helps only partly.
4. **A single score threshold is not the fix.** Historical note, not reproduced by a result file: a sweep of the lower threshold on separate synthetic seeds only traded alignment accuracy and recall for fewer forced matches, and the sweep timed out before the highest values were tried, so those were not evaluated.

## Caveats

* The ambiguity margin was introduced **after** seeing results on development seeds. Development numbers are therefore not a clean held out estimate; they document behaviour after a design change motivated by observed failures. The held out file named above was generated separately.
* Thresholds were tuned on synthetic development seeds only. They are not calibrated on real text. Current values are in `src/taadeel/align.py`.
* Synthetic text is random Arabic word sequences; it does not model legal drafting, cross references, or amendment by reference language.
* The Arabic amendment lexicon is unvalidated (invented samples only). The English amendment pattern module was measured on a small UK sample only.
* The PDF extractor was tested on synthetic PDFs only.
* Point in time correctness is covered only by unit tests on hand built timelines (`tests/test_engine.py`), not by a synthetic evaluation set. It is evaluated on real English UK data in `docs/VALIDATION_UK.md`.
* Moves of an article to a distant position are not supported (monotonic alignment); they surface as repeal plus insert. No test of this limitation has been scored.

## Adversarial cases covered by unit tests

Pure renumbering; «مكرر» articles; orthography only change (diacritics, Arabic-Indic digits) classified `clarified`; a numeric change classified `replaced` and never `clarified`; dissimilar articles with the same number staying unaligned; schema rejects missing provenance and mislabelled synthetic data.

## Required next step to make validation meaningful

Build `data/gold/` from laws with documented amendment histories, hand checked against the official text, each item citing its source. Candidates are listed in `RESEARCH.md` §4. This needs permission to store and use the text (see `DATA_SOURCES.md`).
